title: About
text:
The mapoli Legislative District Atlas was created by Brent Benson who has a passion for collecting, combining, and analyzing data, with a particular interest in Massachusetts politics and policy. You can get in touch with Brent on Bluesky, Threads, or by email using the address brent at mapoli.us.
The primary sources for the data in the district atlas are:

Election results data from the invaluable electionstats.state.ma.us site created by Adam Friedman of Civera and supported by the Secretary of the Commonwealth.
GIS mapping and geometry data from (MassGIS)(https://www.mass.gov/orgs/massgis-bureau-of-geographic-information).
Demographic data from U.S. Census Bureau.

title: mapoli
text:
Interactive maps and demographic data for all 217 Massachusetts legislative districts

State Representative Districts
State Senate Districts
Governor’s Council Districts
U.S. House Districts






While every mapoli State Representative district has approximately the same population (currently about 44,000 people) the districts vary widely in geographic size.
The smallest State Representative district in terms of area is Ways and Means Chair Aaron Michlewitz’s Third Suffolk district coming in at a petite 1.36 square miles.
The largest State Representative district is the Third Berkshire district represented by Leigh Davis of Great Barrington. The district covers a whopping 551 square miles and contains 18 separate municipalities.





The district atlas contains statewide maps for each legislative office with district-to-district comparison tables on political and demographic data.



Example office page





There is also a separate page for each of the 160 State Representative, 40 State Senate, 9 U.S. House, and 8 Governor’s Council districts with demographic details and electon results back to 1990.
